plain_english_policy: This bill establishes a new fee for transferring adult offenders to other states under the Interstate Compact. Specifically, it requires any offender requesting such a transfer to pay a $75 application fee per request. The collected fees are deposited into the State Treasury and continuously appropriated to the Board of Pardons and Paroles to fund the 'Probationer's Upkeep Fund.' However, the bill allows for exemptions from this fee on a case-by-case basis if granted by the Board due to undue hardship.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would create a revenue stream (via transfer fees) specifically designated to support the operational funds of the Pardons and Paroles Board related to probationer upkeep. It formalizes a financial requirement for interstate offender transfers while providing administrative discretion for waivers based on hardship.
sponsorship_supports_position: Senator Means advanced this bill to implement the Interstate Compact fee structure and fund the Probationer's Upkeep Fund.
evidence_quotes: (a) Any adult offender placed under community supervision... filing a written request to transfer residence from this state to another state... shall pay a transfer application fee of seventy-five dollars ($75)... An exemption from the transfer application fee... may be granted by the Board of Pardons and Paroles for undue hardship

(b) The proceeds of the application fees collected pursuant to subsection (a) shall be deposited into the State Treasury to the credit of the Probationer's Upkeep Fund. The funds are hereby continuously appropriated to the Board of Pardons and Paroles.
